However, there are several areas for improvement to enhance clarity and readability. Firstly, the x-axis labels were overlapping, making it difficult to distinguish the years. This was improved by rotating the labels by 45 degrees and right-aligning them. Secondly, the bar placement was adjusted to ensure better spacing and alignment. original_query: Create a bar chart to compare the Preqin Median Net IRR and LN PME Using S&P 500 TR across Vintage years.
optimized_code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.read_csv('table_name.csv')
bar_width = 0.35
index = np.arange(len(df['Vintage']))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))  # Increase figure size for better readability

bar1 = ax.bar(index - bar_width / 2, df['Preqin Median Net IRR'], bar_width, label='Preqin Median Net IRR')
bar2 = ax.bar(index + bar_width / 2, df['LN PME Using S&P 500 TR'], bar_width, label='LN PME Using S&P 500 TR')

plt.xlabel('Vintage Year')
plt.ylabel('Values')
plt.title('Comparison of Preqin Median Net IRR and LN PME Using S&P 500 TR by Vintage Year')

plt.xticks(index, df['Vintage'], rotation=45, ha='right')  # Rotate labels for clarity
plt.legend()
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)  # Add grid for better readability

plt.tight_layout()  # Adjust layout to prevent label clipping
plt.show()
